'''Rudolf Muradovich Muradyan''' ([[Armenian language|Armenian]]: Ռուդոլֆ Մուրադի Մուրադյան; 19 June 1936 – 9 November 2024) was an [[Armenia|Armenian]] [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]]. Rudolf Muradyan's main research relate to theoretical physics, [[Elementary particle physics|elementary-particle physics]], [[cosmology]] and the [[Origin of the universe|origin of the Universe]]. Considering the properties of the interaction of [[Elementary particle|elementary particles]], he proposed the possibility of large-scale [[Invariant (physics)|invariance]] in [[High energy physics|high-energy physics]], from which the "Matveev-Muradyan-Tavkhelidze quark counting rule" is derived especially. He also researched the connection between the appearance of the Universe's [[rotation]] and [[Magnetic field|magnetic fields]] and the [[cosmological constant]]. He is the recipient of the 1988 [[Lenin Prize]], along with [[Albert Tavkhelidze]] and [[Viktor Anatolievich Matveev|Viktor Matveev]], for the discovery of dimensional quark counting rules.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |author= |date=2011 |title=Լրանում է ակադեմիկոս Ռուդոլֆ Մուրադյանի 75-ամյակը |url=http://www.aysor.am/am/news/2011/06/17/rudolf-muradyan/299909 |accessdate=2017-03-20 |publisher=aysor.am |language=hy}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author= |date=2011–2015 |title=Rudolf Muradyan |url=http://www.casinapioiv.va/content/accademia/en/academicians/ordinary/muradyan.html |accessdate=2017-03-20 |publisher=casinapioiv.va |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Rudolf Muradyan was born on June 19, 1936, in [[Yerevan|Yerevan, Armenia]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=LLC |first=Helix Consulting |title=Լրանում է ակադեմիկոս Ռուդոլֆ Մուրադյանի 75-ամյակը - Այսօր' թարմ լուրեր Հայաստանից |url=https://www.aysor.am/am/news/2011/06/17/rudolf-muradyan/299909 |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=www.aysor.am |language=en}}</ref> After [[Graduation|graduating]] from the Yerevan [[Secondary school|Secondary School]] № 25 in 1953, Muradyan entered the Faculty of Physics at [[Moscow State University]] in Moscow, graduating in 1959.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Մուրադյան Ռուդոլֆ Մուրադի (1936-) |url=http://greenstone.flib.sci.am/gsdl/cgi-bin/library.cgi?e=d-01000-00---off-0academic--00-1----0-10-0---0---0direct-10---4------..-0-1l--11-en-50---20-help---00-3-1-00-0--4--0--0-0-11-10-0utfZz-8-00&a=d&c=academic&cl=CL1&d=HASH43b1c99f3b93b839c2a3ec |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=greenstone.flib.sci.am}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Список выпускников 1959 г. |url=http://upmsu.phys.msu.ru/abc1959.html |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=upmsu.phys.msu.ru}}</ref>  In 1962 he finished his [[Postgraduate education|postgraduate study]] in the Faculty of Physics of [[Moscow State University]] and defended his thesis for a PhD in [[Physics]] and [[Mathematics]].<ref name=":1" /> He then worked at the Laboratory of Theoretical Physics of the [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research|Joint Institute of Nuclear Research]] (OIJI) in [[Dubna]] near Moscow between 1962-1979 (from 1966 as a senior research fellow<ref name=":1" />).<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Мурадян Рудольф Мурадович (Дубна) |url=http://dubna.org/p/?id=19524 |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=dubna.org |language=ru}}</ref> In 1970 he was awarded a [[doctorate]] in physical-mathematical sciences and appointed [[professor]]. In 1972 he joined the [[Communist Party of the Soviet Union]].<ref name=":3" /> His scientific papers appeared in ''Theoretical and Mathematical Physics.''<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-10-08 |title=R. M. Muradyan |url=http://65.54.113.26/Author/18898591/r-m-muradyan |access-date=2023-04-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161008140012/http://65.54.113.26/Author/18898591/r-m-muradyan |archive-date=2016-10-08 }}</ref> In 1970 at JINR he defended his [[thesis]] for the degree of Doctor of physical and mathematical sciences, and received the academic rank of [[professor]].<ref name=":3" />

In 1979 Rudolf Muradyan moved to Yerevan, he headed the Department of Radiation Studies of the [[Yerevan Physics Institute]] in 1979-1984.<ref name=":1" /> At the same time he gave special lectures on [[Quantum mechanics|quantum theory]] of solids at the Faculty of Physics of Yerevan State University.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Մուրադյան Ռուդոլֆ Մուրադի (1936-) |url=http://greenstone.flib.sci.am/gsdl/cgi-bin/library.cgi?e=d-01000-00---off-0academic--00-1----0-10-0---0---0direct-10---4------..-0-1l--11-en-50---20-help---00-3-1-00-0--4--0--0-0-11-10-0utfZz-8-00&a=d&c=academic&cl=CL1&d=HASH43b1c99f3b93b839c2a3ec |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=greenstone.flib.sci.am}}</ref> In 1986 Muradyan was elected a corresponding member of the [[Armenian National Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of the Armenian SSR.]]<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Армения |first=Национальная академия наук Республики |title=Национальная академия наук Республики Армения |url=https://www.sci.am//members.php |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Национальная академия наук Республики Армения}}</ref>[[File:Moscow State University crop.jpg|thumb|Moscow State University]]From 1984 to 1994 he worked at [[Byurakan Observatory|Byurakan Astrophysical Observatory]] of Armenian SSR Academy of Sciences (NAS RA) as a [[Leading Researcher]] and since 1985 he worked as a Team Leader.<ref name=":1" /> On October 16, 1994, he was elected an [[academician]] of the [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":2" /> In the same year he moved again to Dubna and worked in the laboratory of theoretical physics of JINR until 1996.<ref name=":4" />

Since 1996 he was professor of the [[Federal University of Bahia|Institute of Physics of the Federal University of Bahia]], [[Salvador, Bahia|Salvador]], [[Brazil]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-09-24 |title=pesquisa |url=http://www.fis.ufba.br/dfes/pesquisa.htm |access-date=2023-04-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924013325/http://www.fis.ufba.br/dfes/pesquisa.htm |archive-date=2015-09-24 }}</ref> In the same year he was elected an academician of the [[Armenian National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences of Armenia]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=National Academy of Sciences of Armenia |url=https://www.sci.am/members.php |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=sci.am}}</ref>

Muradyan died on 9 November 2024, at the age of 88.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rudolf Muradyan |url=https://www.pas.va/en/academicians/deceased/muradyan.html |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=www.pas.va |language=en}}</ref>

== Scientific Work ==
Rudolf Muradyan's main research is in [[theoretical physics]], [[elementary particle physics]], [[High energy physics|high-energy physics]], [[cosmology]] and [[mathematical physics]].<ref name=":1" />

In 1969, based on the [[Quasiparticle|quasi-free quark model]], Rudolf Muradyan, together with [[Albert Tavkhelidze]] and [[Viktor Matveyev|Victor Matveev]], proposed that the scaling properties of high-energy electron-nucleon interaction processes found in experiments are common to all deep inelastic lepton-hadron processes. Muradyan, Tavkhelidze and Matveev have developed an automodelicity (self-similarity) principle on the basis of which these properties may be derived directly. According to this principle, many characteristics of processes in the field of high energies and high momentum transfer, including particle form factors, do not depend on characteristic length and momentum scaling of dimensional parameters. They are homogeneous functions of relativistically invariant kinematical variables and a degree of homogeneity of these functions is determined by their physical dimensionality. A scale law describing the mass spectrum of muon pairs produced at high energies in proton <math>\rho + \rho = \mu^+ + \mu^- +</math> hadrons collisions was first established using the principle of automodelicity:

<math>\frac{d \sigma}{dM^2} \approx \frac{1}{M^4}f\left ( \frac{M}{E} \right )</math>

Where <math>M</math> is the effective mass of the muon pair and <math>E</math> is the energy of the colliding particles. This sweeping law was confirmed in experimental studies begun in 1970 by [[Leon M. Lederman|Leon Lederman's]] group at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory|Brookhaven]]. Subsequently, it was in these processes that a new class of hadrons - <math>J/\Psi</math> particles - were discovered.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=ИЯИ РАН - страница академика А.Н.Тавхелидзе |url=http://www.inr.ru/tavkhelidze/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=www.inr.ru}}</ref>

In 1973, based on the principle of self-similarity, the so-called "Matveev-Muradyan-Tavkhelidze quark counting rules" were established. They define the asymptotics of the form factors at large momentum transfer <math>Q =\sqrt{-t}</math>  as well as the nature of the energy dependence of the differential cross section of an arbitrary binary scattering reaction at large angles at high energies <math>E=\sqrt{s}</math>:

<math>\left ( \frac{d\sigma}{dt} \right )_{ab\rightarrow cd}\approx
\left ( \frac{1}{t} \right )^{n-2}f\left ( \frac{t}{s} \right ) </math>

Where <math>N = N_a + N_b + N_c + N_d</math> is the total number of elementary hadron components participating in the reaction. In this case <math>N_b=1</math> if the particle <math>b</math> is a structureless lepton. The function <math display="inline">f\left ( \frac{t}{s} \right )</math>depends only on the ratio of large kinematic variables. It is a dimensional quantity and the natural scale here is the effective particle size. The power asymptotic law indicates factorization of large and small distance effects.<ref name=":5" /> In 1987 in the State Register of Discoveries of the USSR the discovery (№343) "Rule of quark counting by Matveev-Muradyan-Tavkhelidze" was registered.<ref name=":3" /> In 1970-1980s Rudolf Muradyan together with his colleagues performed a significant cycle of works on application of the automodelicity principle and generalization of quark counting rules for multiple and inclusive processes using a three-dimensional formulation of quantum field theory. According the resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union and Council of Ministers of April 15, 1988, Rudolf Muradyan together with his colleagues was awarded the Lenin Prize for the cycle of studies on the dynamic regularities in the quark structure of elementary particles and atomic nuclei (1965-1977).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rudolf Muradyan |url=https://www.pas.va/en/academicians/ordinary/muradyan.html |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=www.pas.va |language=en}}</ref>

Muradyan investigated the emergence of the Universe, stars, galaxies from an initial hadron, as well as the connection between the appearance of the Universe's rotation and magnetic fields and the cosmological constant <math>\Lambda</math>. In 1976, he discovered a new expression for the angular momentum of the rotation of the Universe:

<math>J=\hbar\left ( \frac{\hbar c}{Gm_p^2} \right )^3</math>

Where <math>\hbar</math> is the Dirac constant, <math>c</math> is the speed of light, <math>G</math> is the gravitational constant, and <math>M_p</math> is the proton mass. Muradyan's proposed hypothesis of the emergence of the Universe, related to [[Viktor Ambartsumian|Victor Hambardzumian's]] theory of the emergence of the Universe, allows to explain the appearance of the rotation of space objects (stars, galaxies and others) in a quantitative way, based on the known relationship in the physics of elementary particles between mass and rotation momentum.<ref name=":1" /> In 1970, Rudolf Muradyan gave an exact solution to the problem of "random walks" on the sphere and in [[Lobachevskian|Lobachevsky space]]. In 1981 he proposed a direct and unified method for constructing irreducible representations for all discrete subgroups of a three-dimensional rotation group, especially for the triangle, tetrahedron and octahedron groups. In 1998, investigating Hopf structures in n-Li - Nambu algebras, he introduced the fundamental concepts of 3-coalgebras, 3-algebras and 3-algebras of Hopf.

In 1990 Rudolf Muradyan proposed the new form of Mendeleev's Periodic Table: the system in which the order of the elements is determined not by the sequence number, but by the structure of the electron shell filling of the atom. This table of elements is based on the quantum-mechanical structure of the atom, and has certain convenience and clarity.<ref name=":0" />
